Learning should reduce corrections

By v/hNovember 27, 2026Document

Originally shared
on LinkedIn

View the post ↗← All journal entries

A lamp that learns should need fewer corrections than a timer.

For the v/h lamp, we want to compare ordinary use with a switch, a fixed schedule and local assistance. The comparison should cover the same varied routine, including an evening that runs late.

We would record unwanted changes to the light, the corrections people make and the time spent setting things up. Ordinary use of the switch should be recorded separately from having to undo an automatic action.

The learning version should reduce effort while leaving people in control of the light. An automatic switch-off only counts as help when the person wanted it.

If a simple timer gives the same benefit with less cost and fewer corrections, we should simplify the design. The local model and supporting hardware have to earn their place in everyday use.

No physical prototype has been built yet. The document describes a proposed comparison, not results from testing.
